name: Randy Scruggs
notes: The live-ensemble producer of the string-band crossover — all-star multi-artist projects tracked with everyone playing at once. Flagship because this is the section's only entry with a first-person method statement, and the research rates it high-medium with the quotes, the console and the project list all sourced. The method is quoted and it converts directly: "my real thrill is there when it's all happening at once", prioritising "the dynamics of several musicians together at the same time" over layering, with a warning against becoming "so technically driven that you start to lose sight of what is being created". The entry's own generator translation is "no per-instrument quantisation, shared timing drift across the ensemble, and dynamics that move together rather than per-track" — which is the humanize block: `quantizeStrength` 0.7 (the loosest in this section), `velocityVar` 0.24, and `timingJitterMs` set to the SAME value on every lane, 9 ms for kick, snare and hat and 10 for percussion, because shared drift means the lanes move together rather than each wandering on its own budget. "Dynamics that move together" is the widest `velocityTiers` spread here — accent 92–118 against main 64–86 — since an un-compressed live room keeps its whole range. The rest of the drum block is the wing's live two-beat: `kick` [1,3] on anchors 1 and 3, hat on quarters and not continuous, four percussion lanes at −7 dB for the string-band room. Keys are the stated string-band G/A/D/C and harmony is "I–IV–V frames, since the repertoire is largely traditional and songwriter material rather than composed pop", so I–IV–V carries weight 6 and `extensions.triad` is 0.8. The arrangement encodes the stated project form: "rotating-guest verse structure (one guest per verse or per section), long instrumental features", i.e. a three-verse structure with an 8–16 bar bridge. ⚠ INFERRED: `bpm.mode` 120 inside the stated 70–200 band, the exact velocity numbers, the 9/10 ms jitter figures (the research says shared drift, not how much), `percs` contents and every melody, countermelody and bassline number. ⚠ The Neve 8232 console owned since 1989 is a sourced fact with no field in this schema and is recorded here rather than encoded.
